claims.claim: **For young people, LARCs are the preferred contraception.** **Add a barrier method such as condoms** to lower STI risk.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contraception' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contraception/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Talking about contraception does not make sexual activity more likely.** Of all groups, adolescents are the least likely to use the most reliable methods.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contraception' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contraception/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Assess and document whether the adolescent is a mature minor with capacity to consent.** Confidentiality applies except where the adolescent is not a mature minor and/or significant risk exists (sexual or physical abuse, harm to self or others).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contraception' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contraception/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Screen for contraindications:** thromboembolism risk, malabsorption, liver disease, and interacting medicines such as enzyme-inducing anti-epileptics.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contraception' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contraception/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine blood pressure and BMI.** Baseline investigations are not usually needed; **consider an STI screen if sexually active and not screened in the last 12 months.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contraception' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contraception/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Explain correct use, side effects and time to efficacy, with written information.** **Review at least 3 months after starting** for adherence, side effects and satisfaction.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contraception' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contraception/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **LARC is the most reliable: with typical use, under 1 pregnancy per 100 women each year.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contraception' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contraception/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Etonogestrel implant (Implanon):** inner upper arm, inserted and removed with local anaesthetic, **lasts up to 3 years**. 20% become amenorrhoeic but 20% have frequent or prolonged bleeding, usually settling within 3 months. ⚠️ **Some enzyme-inducing drugs reduce its efficacy.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contraception' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contraception/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **IUDs (levonorgestrel or copper):** commonly inserted under general anaesthetic in this age group; no drug interactions. ⚠️ **Insertion risks: 1 in 500 uterine perforation, 1 in 300 infection, small risk of expulsion.** ⚠️ **Contraindicated with PID and some STIs.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contraception' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contraception/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mirena LNG-IUD: effective for up to 5 years**, periods shorter and lighter, amenorrhoea in 20% at 1 year. **Kyleena: up to 5 years**, 12% amenorrhoeic at 1 year, more irregular (usually light) bleeding.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contraception' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contraception/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Copper IUD: lasts 5–10 years, varying by type**, no hormonal side effects, but periods may be heavier and more painful.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contraception' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contraception/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Medium reliability: with typical use, 3–7 pregnancies per 100 women each year.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contraception' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contraception/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **First-choice pill in Australia:** low-dose, **35 micrograms or less ethinylestradiol with levonorgestrel or norethisterone** — the 'gold standard' safety profile with low VTE risk; most are on the PBS.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contraception' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contraception/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **COC is not reliable if a dose is missed or taken more than 24 hours late**; vomiting, severe diarrhoea, some medicines and malabsorption reduce efficacy. **Contraindicated in malabsorption and severe liver disease.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contraception' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contraception/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Thrombosis risk factors favour another method:** smoking, raised BMI, immobilisation, thromboembolism or thrombogenic mutations in the patient or family, **migraine with aura**, diabetes with vascular complications, uncontrolled hypertension.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contraception' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contraception/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Vaginal ring (NuvaRing):** in for 3 weeks every month; may be less effective if removed and not reinserted within 24 hours.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contraception' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contraception/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Progestogen-only pill — suitable where oestrogen is not tolerated or is contraindicated.** ⚠️ **Not reliable if taken 3 or more hours late (levonorgestrel/norethisterone POPs) or 24 or more hours late (drospirenone POP).**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contraception' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contraception/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Depot injection every 12 weeks:** 96% effective with typical use; ⚠️ **small decrease in bone density, usually recovering after stopping**; weight gain; periods may take 6–12 months to return.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contraception' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contraception/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Condoms are not reliable contraception but are effective at reducing STI risk** (88% effective with typical use).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contraception' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contraception/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Withdrawal and fertility-awareness methods are not recommended in adolescents.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contraception' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contraception/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consult the paediatric team if a non-consensual relationship or abuse is suspected**; for suspected sexual assault follow local guidelines — **early specialist consultation is vital.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contraception' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contraception/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult adolescent gynaecology** when medical factors affect eligibility or adherence, or menstrual symptoms do not improve on first-line contraception.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contraception' (Last updated October 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contraception/, retrieved 2026-09-23
